subject: physics_2
question_text: Repulsion is the sure test of charging than attraction. Why?

mark_split.label: Attraction is not a sure test

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: a charged body attracts both an oppositely charged body and an uncharged body (by induction), so attraction is ambiguous; repulsion happens only between two like-charged bodies, so it proves charging. Matches the book's answer (printed p.19).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Attraction is not a sure test
lines: A charged body attracts an oppositely
charged body. It also attracts an uncharged
body, by inducing opposite charge on the
near side. So attraction cannot say whether
the other body is charged or uncharged.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name BOTH causes of attraction — opposite charge, and an uncharged body by induction.
steps.why: A test is sure only when one cause can produce it. Attraction has two possible causes, so seeing attraction leaves the question open.
common_mistakes: Saying attraction happens only between opposite charges. An uncharged body is also attracted, by induction.
Leaving out the word induction. It is the reason an uncharged body is attracted.

recall.must_convey: That attraction can come from an oppositely charged body or from an uncharged body by induction, so it is not a sure test.
accept: an uncharged body is also attracted

steps.memory_tip: Attraction has two causes — an opposite charge, or an uncharged body by induction.

steps.label: Repulsion needs like charges
lines: Repulsion happens only between two bodies
with the same kind of charge. An uncharged
body is never repelled. So repulsion is the

lines.text: Only a charged body can be repelled

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The sentence an uncharged body is never repelled closes the argument.
steps.why: Repulsion has exactly one cause — like charges on both bodies. One cause means one conclusion, which is what makes the test sure.
common_mistakes: Writing only like charges repel without adding that an uncharged body is never repelled. Both halves are needed.
Swapping the conclusion — the sure test is repulsion, not attraction.

recall.must_convey: That repulsion happens only between like charges and never with an uncharged body, so repulsion proves charging.
accept: an uncharged body is never repelled
repulsion proves the body is charged

steps.memory_tip: Repulsion has only one cause — like charge on both bodies.

insider_note: The mark-winning sentence is the one the book states only briefly: an uncharged body is also attracted by induction — that is why attraction is not a sure test.
